newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-FRENCH SEEK DOUBLE TRIUMPH OVER ENGLISH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FRENCH SEEK DOUBLE TRIUMPH OVER ENGLISH.

text.p: French clubs hope to do twice in one season what it took them 20 years to do until this week -- to eliminate an English team from European competition.
Holders Paris St German were drawn on Friday to meet Liverpool in the semifinals of the European Cup Winners' Cup, just three days after Monaco put Newcastle United out of the UEFA Cup.
Before Monaco completed a 4-0 aggregate quarter-final victory on Tuesday, the last French club to eliminate an English side had been Bastia in 1977 -- the victims also Newcastle.
"English teams have not given us much success up to now because we were beaten once by Arsenal," PSG executive president Michel Denisot said.
"We start 50-50 but our team, who are very motivated and undoubtedly have a European culture, have a good chance.
"It will be an interesting clash between a more technical football, ours, and a more physical game of contact, Liverpool's," he added.
In the draw held in Lausanne, PSG came out of the hat at home to Liverpool in the first leg on April 10.
Monaco's Brazilian striker Anderson said drawing Italy's Internazionale, for whom former Monaco forward Youri Djorkaeff plays, was what he wanted.

"I hoped we'd get them. Playing the first leg there (in Milan on April 8) is an advantage and also to get a big fish now, right after Newcastle. That will help us stay concentrated and surpass ourselves," Anderson said.
Midfielder Gilles Grimandi believes the meeting with Inter, who have won the trophy twice in the 1990s, is a match worthy of the final.
"Everyone wanted Monaco-Inter in the final but it's a great challenge. We'll be ready," he said.
